title: The Photographer Who Defines the House
author: RN Collins
principle: Evidence leads; atmosphere never substitutes for provenance.

narrativeSequence.caption: A photographer can make a house recognizable by translating garments into light, time, body, setting, and repeatable image grammar; that cultural power does not collapse authorship, copyright ownership, commission terms, credit, or archive custody into one answer.
Gloria Vanderbilt Cooper is retained as evidence, education, reporting or rights context.
narrativeSequence.rights: Included in the Library of Congress Fashion Free to Use and Reuse set; retain Toni Frissell, Vogue context, identifier, and canonical record.

narrativeSequence.caption: 01 · GRAMMAR — What makes the image-world recognizable?. Trace light, distance, movement, lens position, setting, casting, color, sequencing, and refusal across a defined body of work. Describe patterns without claiming the house or photographer owns an abstract style.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 02 · AUTHOR — Who created the photograph?. Preserve photographer, assistants, digital technician, set, styling, model, hair, makeup, retouching, and commissioner records. Under U.S. guidance, do not assume a commission alone answers work-made-for-hire status.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 03 · LICENSE — What may the house actually do?. Attach usage media, territory, term, exclusivity, crops, derivatives, credits, embargoes, archive copies, portfolio uses, and approval language. Route ownership and transfer questions to counsel with the executed agreement.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 04 · MEMORY — Whose archive preserves the house image?. Map negatives or RAW files, selects, contact sheets, captions, model releases, licenses, expiry, publication proofs, and preservation custody. Cultural memory may depend on a record the house does not own.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: Condé Nast Archive is retained as evidence, education, reporting or rights context.
narrativeSequence.rights: Copyright controlled by Condé Nast and creators; licensing required for media.

narrativeSequence.caption: 17 U.S.C. § 201 — Ownership of copyright is retained as evidence, education, reporting or rights context.
